item.text: {"reviews":[{"benchmark":"arc","instrument_review":"ARC-AGI-2 supports comparisons of performance on grid problems under specified evaluation conditions. Worked examples and separate development and evaluation tasks fit its aim of testing how systems infer rules. Human difficulty checks and removal of repeated solution rules strengthen task selection, but matching difficulty for people does not establish equivalent difficulty for AI systems. Scoring is precise: each input requires an exact match within two attempts, and scores average the fraction of inputs solved within each problem. This makes the score interpretable, although it is different from the percentage of whole problems fully solved and gives no credit for partial correctness within a grid. Verified settings and spending limits help comparisons, but single runs, public exposure and revisions limit confidence in small differences or comparisons across testing routes. The supplied evidence supports a focused grid-solving assessment; it does not establish broader intelligence or identify the reasoning process behind a high score.","supported_claims":["The tasks directly require producing new grid outputs from example pairs, supporting assessment of performance on this form of rule inference.","Human solving results informed test selection and difficulty matching, while developer review removed puzzles judged to share solution rules.","Public tasks, scoring software, marking tests and dated revisions make parts of the benchmark inspectable.","Recorded settings and spending limits support comparisons within ARC Prize’s verified evaluation conditions."],"documented_problems":["Exact-match scoring gives a nearly correct grid no credit, limiting what scores reveal about partial progress.","Software awards fractional problem credit, while the published description reserves 'fully solved' for all inputs correct; reporting these as equivalent would mislead.","Verified testing uses one run, so the reported score does not average over repeated-run variation.","Corrections have been necessary, and the change record does not recalculate every affected AI score."],"missing_information":["No repeated-test estimates show how much the same AI’s score varies under identical conditions.","No systematic study establishes sensitivity to instructions, grid presentation or software changes.","The supplied checks do not establish that prior exposure or alternative routes to high scores have been eliminated.","No supplied study links scores to language, social interaction or real-world work; the complete public reporting archive and whole marking system were not independently checked."],"reinterpretations":["Read the score as an average of within-problem exact-input success fractions, not simply the percentage of whole puzzles solved.","Treat human difficulty matching as evidence about human performance, not AI score stability or test-set equivalence for AI.","Treat a high score as successful grid-solving behavior, without assuming it proves a particular reasoning method or general intelligence.","Compare results with attention to test version, exposure, settings, spending limits and evaluation route."],"closing_note":"The review instructions are clear. Benchmark reporting should explicitly distinguish input-level credit from fully solved problems; the change record also documents previously unclear examples."},{"benchmark":"designqa","instrument_review":"DesignQA provides a useful examination of finding and applying Formula SAE rules and interpreting selected vehicle materials. Its practical sources and six task groups support that focused purpose, but one rulebook and uneven question counts provide limited coverage of engineering work. Review by additional readers offers some quality control, although exceptions and unreported disagreement leave answer quality uncertain. Scoring is a major interpretive limitation: wording and formatting can affect credit, and equal weighting of groups combines different marking methods and very different sample sizes. Comparisons also include differences in information supply, so results describe the AI together with its retrieval or document context. The passage-variation experiments offer useful sensitivity evidence but do not establish stability under identical repeated testing. Public materials enable inspection, while incomplete historical records hinder full reproduction. These scores support conclusions about the supplied tasks and conditions, with insufficient evidence for broad engineering competence or confident distinctions between closely ranked systems.","supported_claims":["Real rules, vehicle designs and test data connect the questions to selected engineering activities.","Six question groups cover rule finding, terminology, component recognition, dimensions and performance checks.","Additional reviewers checked many manually written questions, providing some documented quality control.","Experiments changing passages and visual information examine how supplied information affects performance."],"documented_problems":["Question coverage is highly uneven: individual-rule retrieval has 1,192 questions, while performance checking has 16.","Scoring examples show that missing commas and valid related rules absent from reference answers can affect credit.","Systems receive different information, including full rulebooks or retrieved passages, complicating comparisons attributed solely to the AI.","All described scale-bar drawings comply with the rule, allowing an always-yes response to earn decision credit on that portion; no evidence shows an AI used this strategy.","Historical inputs, settings and software are not fully linked to results, and one released answer file has fewer rows than the paper’s corresponding question count."],"missing_information":["Reviewer disagreement rates, remaining answer errors and comprehensive marking accuracy and consistency are not established.","The reviewed evidence does not establish that overall or group scores measure distinct underlying skills.","Identical-condition repeatability and sufficient uncertainty information for small model differences are missing; no human-engineer baseline is reported.","A protected test set, systematic training-overlap checks and clear training and repeated-submission rules were not established.","A clear account of revision effects, a licence file and complete reuse rules were not found in the inspected materials; this does not establish that reuse is prohibited.","Performance on other technical documents or real engineering projects remains unvalidated."],"reinterpretations":["Interpret comparisons as performance of AI systems together with their information supply and evaluation settings.","Read the overall score as an equal-weight combination of six differently scored groups, not as question-level accuracy or a demonstrated general competence measure.","Treat text-similarity credit as an imperfect indicator of answer quality because acceptable wording and reference coverage can affect it.","Treat the five passage-set trials as sensitivity to changed inputs, not repeatability of an identical test.","Interpret the 16-question performance group cautiously: one correct answer changes accuracy by 6.25 percentage points."],"closing_note":"The review instructions are clear. For benchmark answers, expectations about acceptable formatting, additional valid rules and explanation wording need clarification because these can affect credit."}]}
